# SPD-087 — Bash hook Law 7: GIT_WRITE_VERBS misses git's own synonyms (git stage = add, git init-db = init) and its plumbing write verbs

## Brief
Law 7 refuses a spudagent a fixed list of verbs, but git dispatches several of its own commands to the same code under another name, and its plumbing writes the working tree and the object database under names the list does not hold. A member runs 'git stage .' today -- git's own synonym for 'git add', with the same usage line -- and 'git init-db <dir>', its synonym for 'git init'. Beyond the synonyms, 'git checkout-index -a -f' overwrites every tracked file in the working tree (it rewrote the whole tree into a scratch directory in the SPD-049 probe with --prefix), and read-tree, update-index, write-tree, commit-tree, hash-object -w, merge-file, repack, pack-refs, fast-import, unpack-objects, index-pack, sparse-checkout, maintenance, fsck-objects, replay, merge-index, merge-one-file, merge-ours, merge-recursive*, merge-subtree, subtree, send-pack, receive-pack and update-server-info each write the index, the object database or the working tree. SPD-049 closed the options and variables that name a file git writes; this is the verb table itself, one level up, and it is a plain Law 7 bypass rather than a path-rule one.

Evidence: Probed on git 2.54.0 (Apple Git-157) in this worktree, SPD-049: 'git stage -h' prints 'usage: git add [<options>] [--] <pathspec>...' and 'git init-db -h' prints 'usage: git init [-q | --quiet] [--bare] ...'; neither name is in syntax.GIT_WRITE_VERBS, so git_refused returns None and the Bash hook is silent for a member. 'git checkout-index -a --prefix=<dir>/' wrote the entire tree (.claude/, bin/, CLAUDE.md, ledger/, tests/ ...) into the scratch directory, and 'git read-tree HEAD' with GIT_INDEX_FILE wrote a 44 KB index. 'git --list-cmds=main' on this Mac lists all of the names above. Fix sketch: add git's synonyms and the plumbing write verbs to syntax.GIT_WRITE_VERBS (bin/spudlib/shell/syntax.py), with a probe per verb showing what it writes, the way SPD-049 documented its own table.

## Outcome
Law 7 now reads git by an allowlist: syntax.GIT_MEMBER_VERBS names the 64 verbs a member may run and git_verbs.git_not_allowed refuses the other 79 names git knows, against 31 before, so git's own spellings (stage, init-db) and the plumbing that writes the index, the object database or the working tree are closed, and a verb a later git adds is refused until someone reads it. The allowlist is read after Law 7's own table and after SPD-047, so each refusal keeps its reason, and the newly refused verbs stay out of GIT_WRITE_VERBS so their SPD-049 write targets still bind Spud. Suite 886 green in 599 s; hook timing within 0.25 ms of main on every case. Landed as b4590d0; CLAUDE.md Law 7 and .claude/agents/spudagent.md follow in 5d8c619. SPD-093 filed from Cherie's proposal.
